newsitem.title: DUBAI: Bankers give Saudi Ibn Rushd $850mln loan terms.
newsitem.headline: Bankers give Saudi Ibn Rushd $850mln loan terms.

text.p: Bankers on Thursday gave details of the terms of an $850 million loan to a Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) affiliate to partly finance its Ibn Rushd petrochemical project.

The loan has a ten-year life and is priced at 82.5 basis points over LIBOR prior to the project's completion and 77.5 points over after completion. The forecast completion date for the project is June 30, 2000, bankers said.

The loan will have two tranches. The first will be for $600 million and will be drawn in dollars. The second, for $250 million, will be available in a mix of dollars and riyals, allowing the borrower to choose which currency it prefers.

On Wednesday SABIC said it had signed the loan agreement with a consortium of local, regional and international banks to partly-finance the construction of Arabian Industrial Fibers Company (Ibn Rushd) in Yanbu.
Ibn Rushd is 47.96 percent owned by SABIC. The petrochemicals complex is expected to cost around $1.9 billion.

The banks are Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank, Arab National Bank -- partly owned by Jordan's Arab Bank -- Arab Petroleum Investment Corp, Barclays Bank Plc, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank, Industrial Bank of Japan, JP Morgan and Saudi Cairo Bank.
Arranger Riyad Bank said in a statement the syndicate was oversubscribed by more than 30 percent with over thirty regional and international banks participating in the loan.
